did_you_know.text: Did you know? The period of oppression under the Philistines lasted forty years, after the Israelites continued to do what was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
Did you know? Manoah was from Zorah and belonged to the tribe of Dan, and his wife was barren and had not given birth before the angel’s announcement.

Did you know? Samson was destined to be a Nazirite of God from the womb, and it was said of him that he would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines—not necessarily that he would complete the deliverance by himself.

Did you know? In her report to Manoah, his wife adds that the boy would be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death; the angel’s initial words only said that he would be a Nazirite from the womb.
Did you know? Manoah was not satisfied with the message his wife had heard; instead, he prayed that the man of God would return and teach them how to raise the boy who was to be born.

Did you know? The Nazirite instructions included avoiding anything produced by the vine, wine, intoxicating drink, and every form of uncleanness; these instructions were given to the mother, not only to the future child.

Did you know? At first, Manoah thought the man was someone who could be invited to a meal, but the angel clarified that if a burnt offering was made, it was to be offered to the Lord, not to the angel.
Did you know? When Manoah asked for his name, the angel replied that his name was “Wonderful”—something extraordinary or hidden—and did not give him an ordinary, explicit name.
Did you know? Manoah and his wife understood the visitor’s full identity only after he ascended in the flame of the altar, and then they fell facedown on the ground.
Did you know? Even before Samson’s deeds are described, the Spirit of the Lord began to stir him in the area between Zorah and Eshtaol.
